text:
Sofia Ivanova: Dropping link here for PR review thread: scheduler refactor to make workload signals explicit (PR #18527). Would love eyes on API naming + whether we’re ok with the test changes. https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18527

Noah Patel: Took a pass. Overall direction looks right (signals extracted cleanly), but I’m not sold on the naming:
- `workload_signals` vs `workload_profile` (I think this ends up being “profile” once it’s bucketed?)
- `prompt_len_bucket` being used for both chat + completions. Would rather call it `prefill_tokens_bucket` to avoid future confusion when “prompt” != prefill (tools/messages).
Also one nit: you added `concurrency_hint`—is that “active requests” or “inflight decode streams”? docstring reads like the former.

Marcus Reed: +1 on `prefill_tokens_bucket`. We’ve already seen confusion in the metrics layer where “prompt” gets interpreted as “user prompt only”.

Lena Fischer: I’m ok with `workload_signals` as the raw input set and `workload_profile` as the derived thing. Right now the PR exposes only the derived values, so calling it `workload_profile` might be more accurate.
If we keep `workload_signals`, maybe clarify it’s *already bucketed*.

Julian Moore: From instrumentation perspective: `workload_signals` reads like high-cardinality stuff we’d never want to label in metrics (e.g. exact prompt len). Since this is buckets, I’d vote `workload_profile` too.

Hiro Tanaka: Another naming question: `decode_priority_boost` (new field) — is that equivalent to the old `decode_weight`? The mapping in the PR makes it look like it’s just a rename with different sign semantics.
I’m fine with rename but it should be explicit in the config explain output; otherwise people will think we added a new knob.

Sofia Ivanova: Good feedback.
- Agree re: `prefill_tokens_bucket`
- For `workload_signals` vs `profile`: intention was “signals” are computed in runtime from current state (active slots, queue depth, prefill est), but we intentionally *bucket* them before passing into mapping to keep it stable.
Maybe rename the struct to `WorkloadProfile` and keep internal variable names as signals.

Benji Okafor: quick question on the public config surface: are we exposing any of this in customer config? Or purely internal (for tier mapping)?
If it’s internal, we can be a bit more opinionated. If it’s going to show up in `GET /config/explain`, it should read clean.

Sofia Ivanova: Not directly configurable. But it *will* show up in `config/explain` as “inputs used for tier mapping” (per PR #18470). So naming matters.

Noah Patel: In that case, +1 “profile”. You’ll get less support tickets.
Also: can we avoid “hint” in `concurrency_hint`? It’s not a hint if it’s derived from actual inflight requests.
Maybe:
- `inflight_requests_bucket`
- or `active_sequences_bucket` (if it’s sequences)
But the implementation is pulling from scheduler’s “active requests”, right?

Marcus Reed: Implementation looks like it’s counting request contexts attached to a model runner (prefill+decode). That’s “active requests”, not sequences.

Sofia Ivanova: Yep, it’s active request contexts (1 per request).
I can rename to `active_requests_bucket`.

Leila Farouk: On tests: I see you changed the scheduler unit tests to assert on the new `Workload*` struct + golden mapping outputs.
Two failures in CI are in `integration/test_streaming_cadence_smoke` though. Did that already start flaking or is the refactor changing timing?

ci-bot: Build #982114 failed: `integration/test_streaming_cadence_smoke` (timeout) on runner gpu-a10g-2.
Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/982114

Sahana Iyer: I dug into the CI link. It’s *probably* existing flake, but this PR made it slightly worse by changing the internal scheduling loop to sample queue depth earlier.
In the failing run, decode cadence stalls for ~1.3s and the test trips the “max gap” assertion.
We’ve had this pop up 1/50 even without changes, but now it’s 2/10 on this branch.

Hiro Tanaka: That’s concerning. Is it a real regression or just more variance?
If the refactor moved sampling earlier, it could be biasing the mapping to prefer larger prefill batches and starving decode in some edge cases.

Julian Moore: In the trace from CI: queue delay histogram spikes at the same time. There’s a burst of new prefills, decode threads not getting scheduled.
Feels like we’re missing the decode prioritization guard (the one we added in #18463).

Sofia Ivanova: The PR shouldn’t touch prioritization policy, but it did rearrange where we compute the “pressure” scalar.
I’ll do two things:
1) rerun CI with tracing enabled on that test to confirm we’re not accidentally bypassing `decode_guard_min_share`
2) if it’s only test flake, we can relax the assertion (but would rather not)

Noah Patel: Please don’t relax unless we have a clear reason. That test is the only thing catching streaming cadence issues before perf-canary.

Sahana Iyer: Agree. A low-risk option: add a retry for that one test *only on known flaky runners* is gross, but we’ve done similar.
Better option: make the test deterministic: pin concurrency + seed + disable autoscaling variability.
Right now the harness uses “best effort” warmup which sometimes under-warms.

Leila Farouk: +1 deterministic. I can open a follow-up ticket to fix the harness, but we still need this PR to pass.
Maybe add explicit warmup to the test in this PR?

Marcus Reed: We can also gate the sampling in the refactor behind a feature flag? But that’s kind of pointless since it’s a refactor.
I’d rather fix the ordering to match previous behavior.

Sofia Ivanova: I think I found the culprit. In the refactor, `active_requests_bucket` is computed before we attach the new request context to the runner (so undercounts by 1 in bursts). That pushes mapping to slightly higher `max_batch` and queue delay on the same tick.
For streaming loads, that can cause a micro-starvation window.
Fix: compute profile after admission/attach, or explicitly include the pending admission count.

Hiro Tanaka: That makes sense. Under-counting load -> more aggressive batching -> worse decode cadence. Please fix ordering.

Noah Patel: That also addresses the semantics confusion—if it’s computed “pre-admission”, it really *is* a hint. If post-admission, it’s active.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll change it to compute after attach so `active_requests_bucket` truly reflects active contexts.
Naming changes I’ll do in same push:
- `WorkloadSignals` -> `WorkloadProfile`
- `prompt_len_bucket` -> `prefill_tokens_bucket`
- `concurrency_hint` -> `active_requests_bucket`

github-bot: @SofiaIvanova pushed 3 commits to PR #18527:
- Rename WorkloadSignals -> WorkloadProfile
- Rename prompt_len_bucket -> prefill_tokens_bucket
- Compute workload profile post-admission to avoid undercount in burst

ci-bot: Build #982201 started for PR #18527.

Julian Moore: ty. For `config/explain`, can we ensure we print the bucket boundaries somewhere? Otherwise “prefill_tokens_bucket=2” is meaningless.
Even a static string like `prefill_tokens_bucket=[0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049+]`.

Sofia Ivanova: Yep, that’s in PR #18470 but I’ll add a TODO comment pointing to it + ensure the enum values match.

Sahana Iyer: Build #982201 looks better so far. Streaming cadence test passed on first try.
One more suggestion: add a small unit test asserting the profile is computed after attach (regression guard). Otherwise we’ll reintroduce this later.

Marcus Reed: +1. Something like “admission increments active count before profile snapshot”.

Sofia Ivanova: Added in latest commit (tiny scheduler test). CI should pick it up.

ci-bot: Build #982201 succeeded.

Leila Farouk: Nice. Approving on my side once you resolve the last nit comment about docstrings.

Noah Patel: LGTM after naming changes. Please update the docstring where it says “prompt length” (now prefill tokens). Approving once that’s done.

Sofia Ivanova: Done. Merged docstring fixes.

github-bot: PR #18527 merged into main by @SofiaIvanova.

Hiro Tanaka: Thanks all. Can we track the streaming cadence flake separately? It’s not fully gone, just less frequent.

Sahana Iyer: Yeah, I’ll file a CI reliability ticket + propose making that test deterministic. Will link it here once created.

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup: (also will mention in runtime-1.21 release notes that this refactor is no functional change, but adds explicit profile logging for tier mapping).
